investor_summary: The official NAV moved from 2260.525 to 2207.727 for the week ended 15 September 2026, a decline of about 2.336%, while approximate equity impact was -1.178%. The equity impact of -1.178% indicates the portfolio’s equity allocation was the principal driver of the weekly decline. The main drag came from financials and select consumer and IT names, with banking stocks pressured by funding-cost and margin concerns. The financial sector accounted for several of the largest drags, as margin pressure and funding concerns dominated bank news flow. ICICI Bank Ltd. fell about 3.5% as rising FCNR(B) deposit costs by 15-20 bps threatened net interest margins and banks sought longer-term overseas funding. State Bank of India fell about 3.97% as FCNR(B) deposit cost rise, a bank strike that disrupted public sector operations, and banks seeking foreign loans weighed on sentiment. InterGlobe Aviation Ltd. fell about 4.48% after India retail inflation hit a 20-month high of 4.82%, increasing rate-hike risk and squeezing discretionary spending. Axis Bank Ltd. fell about 2.02% as a foreign investor allocation rejig suggested reallocation away from Indian financials, management warned about abnormal lending from record FCNR deposit inflows, and FCNR(B) deposit costs rose. Maruti Suzuki India Limited fell about 3.24% on vehicle shortage ahead of the festive season, implying lost sales momentum. SBI Life Insurance Company Ltd. fell about 2.51% and hit a 52-week low, reflecting broad selling pressure and negative momentum. Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited fell about 2.25% as FCNR(B) deposit cost rise threatened interest margins, a sector headwind. HCL Technologies Ltd. fell about 1.82% as it extended a losing streak and the IT index selloff weighed on the stock. Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. fell about 1.11% amid a broad market sell-off driven by elevated crude oil prices and global bond yields. Bharti Airtel Ltd. fell about 0.53% after Vodafone Idea secured $3.5B debt financing, improving a competitor’s ability to compete. On the offset side, HDFC Bank rose about 1.93% as CEO succession candidates moved to RBI, a foreign investor allocation rejig pointed to inflows into Indian financials, and banking system liquidity glut supported sentiment. The only named offset was HDFC Bank, which helped cushion the fall but did not fully offset the broader weakness. Eicher Motors Ltd. fell about 3.81% without a clear news catalyst, so the move looks like price or flow action rather than a news-driven event.
